presentation.label: digichain
presentation.summary: What Digi Mono and Digi Poly build on: their SRC pages, knob graphics and menu icons. Not with DIGISLICER, NEIGHBOR or SOPHIE.
presentation.overview: digichain is a framework other mods build on. SOPHIE, NEIGHBOR and DIGISLICER each patch some of the same SRC-page places (knob labels, values, graphics and ranges) and the same render step, and elekloader allows one owner per byte. digichain owns each of those places once and passes each call to the mod whose machine it is for, or to the stock code. Digi Mono and Digi Poly get their SRC page through it too, Digi Mono its LFO page’s DEST names as well, and the FUNC + SRC list draws every added machine’s icon. The author’s description also covers the -chain builds of SOPHIE, NEIGHBOR and DIGISLICER that the author’s own tools make for it; Modwerk carries those mods as their authors built them, and its builder refuses them beside digichain. It adds no sound, page or control, and changes nothing on its own.
highlights: One owner for SRC-page and render places that several mods patch; each call goes to the machine it is for, or to the stock code.
Digi Mono’s SRC page layout, knob graphics, UI records and knob values, and Digi Poly’s POLY page layout, come through it.
Digi Mono’s LFO DEST names come through it; every other machine keeps the firmware’s names.
Every added machine shows its own icon in the FUNC + SRC list; core 2.1 alone drew only the first.
Adds no sound, page or control, and changes nothing on its own.
usage: Build it with Digi Mono or Digi Poly: both require it.
Press FUNC + SRC on an audio track to see each added machine with its own icon.

access.location: No page of its own; it works behind the SRC pages, the LFO page and the FUNC + SRC machine list
steps: Build digichain with Digi Mono or Digi Poly, which require it; on its own it changes nothing.
On an audio track, press FUNC + SRC: every added machine shows its own icon in the list.
Choose a Digi Mono machine or POLY: its SRC page, and for Digi Mono its LFO page’s DEST names, come through digichain.

limitations: Modwerk’s builder refuses digichain beside NEIGHBOR, DIGISLICER and SOPHIE: elekloader finds that their patch sites overlap. The -chain builds of those three, which the author’s tools/dev.sh makes to route through digichain, are not in Modwerk.
Built for Digitakt OS 1.53 and 1.54.
It changes nothing on its own: it routes calls for the mods that build on it, in Modwerk Digi Mono and Digi Poly.
Its NEIGHBOR behaviour (SLOT limited to 0–8, a new NEIGHBOR track taking the track on its left as its source) needs NEIGHBOR in the build, so it does not apply to a Modwerk build.
Not yet tested on a unit, its author reports; it passes the author’s emulator tests on OS 1.53 and 1.54.

claims: param:SRC page hooks shared by SOPHIE, NEIGHBOR and DIGISLICER

load.conditions: Measure with every track playing Digi Mono or POLY machines and their SRC and LFO pages open with knobs turning, since every routed call passes through it.

presentation.label: Digi EQ
presentation.summary: A 4-band master EQ on every output (main outs, headphones and USB), per pattern.
presentation.overview: Digi EQ is a 4-band EQ on the master mix, before the render hands it to the analog outputs and to the USB stream, so main outs, headphones and USB audio all carry it, as they do the compressor. It is a master page (FUNC + LFO) between Compressor and Internal Mixer: knobs A-D set the bands’ levels and E-H their frequencies, and a press switches a knob to its band’s Q or type. The response curve is drawn above the knobs. The settings live in the pattern’s kit, so every pattern has its own EQ, saved with the project and kept over a power-off. SETTINGS > GLOBAL FX/MIX > MASTER EQ makes the EQ you can hear override every pattern’s own.
highlights: A 4-band EQ on the master mix: main outs, headphones and USB audio all carry it.
Its own master page, Master EQ (2/4), between Compressor and Internal Mixer, with the response curve drawn above the knobs.
Seven band types: HP, low shelf, bell, notch, band pass, high shelf and LP.
Each pattern has its own EQ, kept in its kit, saved with the project and kept over a power-off.
SETTINGS > GLOBAL FX/MIX > MASTER EQ makes the EQ you can hear override every pattern’s own.
Bell and shelf bands at 0 dB cost nothing.
usage: Give each pattern its own master tone: the EQ is saved with the pattern’s kit, and loading a sound onto a track leaves it as it is.
Turn on MASTER EQ in SETTINGS > GLOBAL FX/MIX to carry one EQ across every pattern, and save the project to keep it in those patterns.
If you hear clicks in a busy project, set bands back to 0 dB and away from the filter types, or turn on digihealth’s FAST AUDIO for headroom.
When boosting, lower the master volume or cut elsewhere: the output is limited to full scale.
On the unit, check once after a power cycle that a pattern’s EQ came back.

access.location: Master pages (FUNC + LFO): Master EQ (2/4), between Compressor and Internal Mixer
steps: Press FUNC + LFO for the master pages; FUNC + LFO steps through Compressor (1/4), Master EQ (2/4), Internal Mixer (3/4) and External Mixer (4/4).
Turn knobs A-D for the bands’ levels and E-H for their frequencies; bands 1-4 are the columns A/E, B/F, C/G and D/H.
Press a knob to switch it to its band’s Q (A-D) or type (E-H); press it again to go back.
For one EQ on every pattern, turn on SETTINGS > GLOBAL FX/MIX > MASTER EQ.

controls.name: Knobs A-D
controls.doc: Band 1-4 level, -12 to +12 dB in 0.5 dB steps (band 1 on A, band 4 on D); every band starts at 0 dB. For BELL and the shelves it is the boost or cut; for HP, LP, BP and NTCH it is that band’s output level, and the band is always on. Press the knob for the band’s Q.

controls.name: Knobs A-D, pressed
controls.doc: Band 1-4 Q, 0.3 to 8 in 16 steps; for HP, LP, BP and NTCH it is the resonance. A switched knob is shown inverted. Press the knob again to go back to the level.

controls.name: Knobs E-H
controls.doc: Band 1-4 frequency, 20 Hz to 20 kHz in 128 steps, about a semitone a notch (band 1 on E, band 4 on H). Defaults: band 1 78 Hz, band 2 398 Hz, band 3 2.5 kHz, band 4 9.9 kHz. Press the knob for the band’s type.

controls.name: Knobs E-H, pressed
controls.doc: Band 1-4 type: HP, LSHF (low shelf), BELL, NTCH (notch), BP (band pass), HSHF (high shelf) or LP. HP, LP, BP and NTCH are 12 dB/octave. Defaults: band 1 low shelf, bands 2 and 3 bell, band 4 high shelf. Press the knob again to go back to the frequency.

controls.name: MASTER EQ
controls.doc: SETTINGS › GLOBAL FX/MIX › MASTER EQ, beside the firmware’s own entries. On: the EQ you can hear overrides every pattern’s own, and each pattern you reach is given these settings, so save the project if you want them kept. Off: every pattern goes back to its own saved EQ.

limitations: The builder refuses no pairing: in elekloader’s check Digi EQ combines with every other Modwerk mod for its OS, NEIGHBOR, DIGISLICER and SOPHIE among them.
Built for OS 1.53 and 1.54.

Four active bands cost about 5 % of the audio time, by the author’s estimate; in a very busy project that could push the audio over its budget and cause clicks. Bell and shelf bands at 0 dB cost nothing; HP, LP, BP and NTCH bands are always on.
Boosts can clip the main output, which is limited to full scale.

The settings are kept in bytes of the first four tracks’ sound records that the firmware saves and loads but does not use itself. If the firmware used them somewhere the author’s emulator tests did not reach, a setting could be lost or a sound could change.
With MASTER EQ on, every pattern the unit reaches is given the current EQ settings, which changes those patterns’ kits; the change becomes permanent only when you save the project.
The page is an extra entry in the firmware’s master view (its unused “None” page, renamed); the author notes that an untested path of that view could treat it differently.
Its author reports Digi EQ 1.0b is not yet tested on a unit; it passes their emulator tests on OS 1.53 and 1.54.

load.conditions: Measure with every track playing, parameters modulated and all four EQ bands active (away from 0 dB, or set to HP, LP, BP or NTCH), the mod’s heaviest setting, on OS 1.53 and 1.54.

tests.summary: Modwerk’s elekloader builder linked and verified a build of Digi EQ 1.0b with core 2.1 for OS 1.53 and 1.54; nothing was flashed or tested on hardware, and the evidence tier is none.

presentation.label: DIGIHEALTH
presentation.summary: FAST AUDIO lowers the DSP load; SYSTEM INFO shows CPU, DSP and memory in the top bar.
presentation.overview: digihealth adds FAST AUDIO and SYSTEM INFO to SETTINGS on the original Digitakt. FAST AUDIO runs the audio renderer’s existing hot code from on-chip SRAM; it changes where the code runs, rather than the sound. It normally starts about two seconds after the screen appears. SYSTEM INFO alternates CPU/audio-render load and free RAM/sample memory in the top bar. Its DSP figure describes the audio render, not the cost of a single module. A read-only USB SysEx diagnostics channel uses device byte 0x7D.
highlights: FAST AUDIO uses the existing render code in SRAM, with a checksum watchdog and fallback to stock code.
SYSTEM INFO alternates load and memory pages every two seconds, including the last second’s DSP peak.
The optional USB diagnostics channel reads status without changing settings or memory.
usage: Open SETTINGS, tick SYSTEM INFO, then return to a pattern with samples already loaded.
Play the pattern. Watch CPU and DSP current/peak load, then wait for the free RAM and sample-memory page; the pages alternate every two seconds.
Keep the pattern unchanged and untick FAST AUDIO in SETTINGS. Compare several readouts of the same passage; any difference depends on the workload.
Stop playback and untick SYSTEM INFO to hide the readout. FAST AUDIO stays disabled until the next power-on; its watchdog may also refuse or undo the SRAM copy.

steps: Use a build containing digihealth for the original Digitakt on OS 1.53 or 1.54.
Open SETTINGS and tick SYSTEM INFO to show the readout in the top bar.
FAST AUDIO normally starts automatically after boot; untick its SETTINGS row to disable it for this power-on.

controls.name: FAST AUDIO
controls.doc: Runs the existing audio-render code from SRAM. Normally starts about two seconds after boot; unticking disables it until the next power-on. It refuses a nonempty SRAM area, and its checksum watchdog returns to stock code if the copy is overwritten.

controls.name: SYSTEM INFO
controls.doc: Shows alternating two-second top-bar pages: CPU load and audio-render DSP current/last-second peak, then free heap RAM and sample memory. Untick to hide the display; these are whole-workload readings, not a per-module benchmark.

limitations: FAST AUDIO’s call-site stubs are derived from the owner’s stock OS file. Modwerk generates them during the local build, never in CI.

load.conditions: Measure with every track playing, parameters modulated and the mod at its heaviest setting.

tests.summary: Imported from the author’s v1.1 source; Modwerk linked and verified the pinned catalog release for the UI documentation run. Documentation captures verify the listed UI pages on OS 1.53; audio, timing and hardware remain unqualified.

Stop playback and untick SYSTEM INFO to hide the readout. FAST AUDIO stays disabled until the next power-on; its watchdog may also refuse or undo the SRAM copy.

presentation.label: Digi Matrix
presentation.summary: A modulation matrix: any track's LFO to any parameter of any track, in 8 slots, per pattern.
presentation.overview: Digi Matrix is a modulation matrix for the LFOs of the original Digitakt. Stock, each of a track’s two LFOs modulates one parameter of its own track. SETTINGS > MOD MATRIX adds a page of 8 routing slots; each sends any track’s LFO1 or LFO2 to any parameter of any track, with its own depth from -64 to +64, so one LFO can drive several parameters across several tracks by different amounts. Per slot, OWN says whether the LFO still modulates its own track’s DEST as well. The matrix lives in the pattern’s kit, so each pattern has its own and it is saved with the project.
highlights: 8 routing slots, each sending any track’s LFO1 or LFO2 to any parameter of any track.
Each slot has its own depth, -64 to +64; the LFO’s own DEP keeps controlling only its own track.
OWN per slot: the LFO still modulates its own track’s DEST as well, or only what the matrix routes it to.
Destinations on the destination track’s SRC, filter, AMP and LFO pages.
Kept in the pattern’s kit: each pattern has its own matrix, saved with the project and kept over a power cycle.
The author measured the whole matrix at about 0.4 % of the audio time, even with all 8 slots on.
usage: Send one LFO to several parameters on several tracks, each by a different amount.
Route one track’s LFO to another track’s filter, as in the author’s example T1 L2 > T4 FLT.FREQ.
Let one LFO modulate the other one’s speed or depth with the L1.* and L2.* destinations.
Set X under OWN to use an LFO only through the matrix, not on its own track.
Shape the source LFO as usual on its own track’s LFO page: SPD, MULT, WAVE, PHAS, FADE and trig MODE.
Give each pattern its own routings; changing pattern changes the matrix.

steps: Open SETTINGS and go to the MOD MATRIX row; it shows how many of the 8 slots are on.
Press YES on the row to open the page of 8 routing slots.
Choose a slot with UP/DOWN or the LEVEL knob and press YES to turn it on.
Set the slot with knobs A–F; NO leaves the page.

controls.name: UP / DOWN or LEVEL
controls.doc: Choose one of the 8 slots; the slot under the cursor is shown inverted.

controls.name: YES
controls.doc: Turn the slot under the cursor on, or off again. A slot switched on for the first time starts on the cursor’s own track: slot 3 routes track 3’s LFO1 to track 3. The knobs edit only a slot that is on.

controls.name: NO
controls.doc: Leave the MOD MATRIX page.

controls.name: Knob A
controls.doc: Source track, 1–8.

controls.name: Knob B
controls.doc: Source LFO, 1 or 2 (L1 or L2 on the page).

controls.name: Knob C
controls.doc: Destination track, 1–8.

controls.name: Knob D
controls.doc: Destination parameter, named by its page: SRC.A to SRC.H (the track’s SRC page, whatever its machine calls them); FLT.TYPE, FREQ, RESO, ENV, ATK, DEC, SUS and REL; FLT2.A to FLT2.E (the second filter page); AMP.ATK, HOLD, DEC, OVER, DEL, REV, PAN and VOL; and L1.* and L2.*, so an LFO can modulate the other one’s speed, depth and so on.

controls.name: Knob E
controls.doc: Depth, -64 to +64, 2 a notch. Each slot has its own depth, independent of the source LFO’s own DEP, which keeps controlling only its own track’s modulation.

controls.name: Knob F
controls.doc: OWN: whether the source LFO still modulates its own track’s DEST as well (blank), or only what the matrix routes it to (X).

limitations: Modwerk’s builder refuses no mod beside it: in elekloader’s check it combines with every other Modwerk mod for its OS, NEIGHBOR, DIGISLICER and SOPHIE included (SOPHIE is built for OS 1.53 only).
Built for OS 1.53 and 1.54.

SRC.A to SRC.H follow whatever the destination track’s machine puts on those knobs; the page names them by page and knob, so the author advises picking them with that track’s SRC page in front of you.
A trig-mode source LFO moves only when its own track trigs.

The matrix is kept in six bytes of each sound record that the firmware saves and loads but does not use itself; the author asks owners to check once, after a power cycle on a unit, that a pattern’s matrix came back.
Not yet tested on a unit, its author reports; it passes their emulator tests on OS 1.53 and 1.54.

load.conditions: Measure with all 8 slots on at non-zero depth, every track playing and its LFOs running, the mod’s heaviest setting.

Machine and parameter names after the Monomachine manual; vowel formants from Peterson and Barney (1952)

presentation.label: Digi Mono
presentation.summary: Seven synth machines after the Monomachine: sine, noise, saw, pulse, an ensemble, a formant voice and a three-sine chord, each with its own SRC page.
presentation.overview: Digi Mono adds seven synth machines to the FUNC+SRC list, after the Monomachine’s GND and SWAVE machines: MONO SIN, MONO NOISE, MONO SAW, MONO PULSE, MONO ENS, MONO VO and POLY SIN. They need no sample: the engine’s output takes the sample’s place in the voice, so the track’s filter, amp, LFOs, sends, p-locks and level work on it as on a sample. Knob A stays TUNE; B to H are the machine’s own parameters, named and shown in their units. The engine is a clean-room rewrite from the Monomachine manual, with no Monomachine code or data.
highlights: Seven machines, each with its own icon: MONO SIN, MONO NOISE, MONO SAW, MONO PULSE, MONO ENS, MONO VO and POLY SIN.
Each machine’s SRC page names its knobs and shows values in their units: semitones, %, ms, vowels and consonants.
No sample needed; the FLTR, AMP and LFO pages, sends and p-locks work as on a sample track.
MONO VO is a formant voice: one vowel gliding to another, with consonants at the note’s start.
POLY SIN plays three sines at set notes, a chord on one track, with a pitch envelope.
An LFO’s DEST names the machine’s own knobs, for example MSAW:Unison Level.
A clean-room engine: no Monomachine code or data.
usage: Pick a machine with FUNC+SRC on an audio track, scrolling past SLICE and any other mod’s machines; YES confirms.
Play it from trigs, the track key, the keyboard (FUNC+TRK) or MIDI, like a sample track; the note and TUNE set the pitch.
Set the volume with the track’s LEVEL, the AMP page and VOL.
Keep to a few playing Digi Mono tracks; VO, ENS and PULSE cost the most. Check the load with digihealth’s SYSTEM INFO.
MONO ENS starts with its chorus off (CHRL 0) and MONO VO without a consonant; turning them on costs more.
The author’s load test in docs/USAGE.md adds one playing track at a time while watching DSP and its peak.

access.location: SRC machine list, after SLICE and any other mod’s machines
steps: Select an audio track, press FUNC + SRC and scroll past SLICE (and any other mod’s machines).
Choose MONO SIN, MONO NOISE, MONO SAW, MONO PULSE, MONO ENS, MONO VO or POLY SIN and press YES.
On the SRC page, knob A is TUNE and B to H are the machine’s own parameters; a knob the machine does not have is blank.
Play it from trigs, the track key, the keyboard (FUNC + TRK) or MIDI.

controls.name: Knob A
controls.doc: TUNE on every Digi Mono machine. With the note it sets the pitch; note locks, TUNE locks and pitch LFOs work.

controls.name: Knob B
controls.doc: Differs per machine. NOISE: ST (Sample Hold Rate), sample and hold, 0 = white, higher = fewer new values a second. SAW and PULSE: UNIL (Unison Level), the unison oscillators’ level. ENS: PCH2 (Pitch Osc 2), oscillator 2 in semitones from oscillator 1, -36..+36. VO: VOC1 (Vowel 1): OO, U, AW, AH, UH, AE, EH, IH, EE or ER. POLY SIN: NOT1 (Note 1), the first sine in semitones from the note, -36..+36. Blank on SIN.

controls.name: Knob C
controls.doc: Differs per machine. NOISE: RED (Red Noise), darker noise. SAW and PULSE: UNIW (Unison Detune), the unison detune, 0..50 cents. ENS: PCH3 (Pitch Osc 3), oscillator 3 in semitones. VO: VOC2 (Vowel 2), the vowel V-SW glides to. POLY SIN: NOT2 (Note 2), the second sine in semitones from the note. Blank on SIN.

controls.name: Knob D
controls.doc: Differs per machine, and does not open the sample list on these machines. PULSE: SUB2 (Sub 2 Oct Lev), the sub two octaves down. ENS: PW (Pulse Width), duty %, 0 = square. VO: VOIC (Breath), breath noise mixed into the source. POLY SIN: NOT3 (Note 3), the third sine in semitones from the note. Blank on SIN, NOISE and SAW.

controls.name: Knob E
controls.doc: Differs per machine. NOISE: STON (Tuned Noise), a sample and hold at twice the note’s pitch, which makes the noise pitched. SAW: UNIX (Unison Voices), 1 to 3 unison saws. PULSE: SUB1 (Sub 1 Oct Lev), the sub one octave down. ENS: PCH4 (Pitch Osc 4), oscillator 4 in semitones. VO: V-SW (Vowel Glide), the glide from VOC1 to VOC2, 5 ms..2 s; 0 keeps VOC1. POLY SIN: EDEP (Env Depth), the pitch envelope’s depth in semitones, + or -. Blank on SIN.

controls.name: Knob F
controls.doc: Differs per machine. SAW: SUBX (Sub Shape), the subs from square to saw, in %. PULSE: PW (Pulse Width), duty %. ENS: WAVE (Saw-Pulse), saw to pulse, in %. VO: CONS (Consonant): none, S, SH, F, H, T, K or P at the note’s start. POLY SIN: ESPD (Env Speed), the pitch envelope’s speed: + glides back to the notes, - glides away, OFF in the middle. Blank on SIN and NOISE.

controls.name: Knob G
controls.doc: Differs per machine. SAW: SUB1 (Sub 1 Oct Lev), the sub one octave down. PULSE: PWAD (PWM Depth), the pulse width modulation depth. ENS: CHRL (Chorus Level); it starts at 0, the chorus off. VO: CLEN (Cons. Length), the consonant’s length, 2..400 ms (T, K and P at most 30-40 ms). Blank on SIN, NOISE and POLY SIN.

controls.name: Knob H
controls.doc: Differs per machine. SAW: SUB2 (Sub 2 Oct Lev), the sub two octaves down. PULSE: PWRS (PWM Rate), 0.05..20 Hz. ENS: CHRW (Chorus Width). VO: CVOL (Cons. Level), the consonant’s level. Blank on SIN, NOISE and POLY SIN. The volume is the track’s LEVEL, AMP page and VOL, not this knob.

limitations: Modwerk’s builder refuses Digi Mono beside NEIGHBOR, DIGISLICER and SOPHIE: elekloader finds that their patch sites overlap those of DIGICHAIN, which Digi Mono needs. The author pairs them through -chain builds of those mods, which are not the releases Modwerk carries.
Built for Digitakt OS 1.53 and 1.54.

On a unit the stock audio engine already uses about 80 % of each block, so keep to a few playing Digi Mono tracks. The author’s design notes give two to four at once as the safe range until it is measured on a unit; VO, ENS and PULSE cost the most.
A project saved with Digi Mono machines loads them as ONESHOT on the stock OS, or on a build without Digi Mono.
A POLY SIN sound saved with 0.13 or 0.13a reads its old NOT3 as EDEP and its EDEP as ESPD; set them again.
The engine follows the Monomachine manual’s descriptions; it is not sample-exact to a Monomachine.
Not yet tested on a unit, its author reports; it passes their emulator tests on OS 1.53 and 1.54.

claims: param:SLICE page names, ranges and values while a Digi Mono machine is active

load.conditions: Measure with every track playing a Digi Mono machine at its heaviest setting (MONO VO with a consonant, MONO ENS with the chorus and WAVE on), parameters modulated, reading DSP and its peak in digihealth’s SYSTEM INFO.

tests.summary: Modwerk’s builder linked and verified a build with core 2.1 and DIGICHAIN 1.6 on OS 1.53 and 1.54; nothing was flashed or tested on hardware, and the evidence tier is none.

presentation.label: NEIGHBOR
presentation.summary: A NEIGHBOR machine like the Octatrack’s: a track plays another track’s audio through its own chain. A prototype.
presentation.overview: NEIGHBOR replaces a sample source with another audio track’s post-filter signal on the original Digitakt. Choose the receiving track with FUNC + SRC, set SLOT to the source track, and trigger the receiving track so its AMP envelope opens. The incoming signal passes through the receiving track’s overdrive, bit reduction, filter, envelope, volume, pan and sends. The source is tapped before its volume, so lowering the source’s AMP VOL removes the dry mix without cutting the routed signal. Routing adds one 32-sample block (about 0.67 ms); nonzero pitch shifting adds further latency. This remains an upstream prototype.
highlights: SLOT selects source track 1–8; zero or the receiving track itself produces silence.
TUNE shifts up to two octaves either way and follows trig notes; neutral pitch bypasses the shifter.
LEV drives the receiving chain; GAIN adds up to +31.5 dB after that chain and before its volume.
Receiving-track trigs and AMP settings gate the source; the original track can remain in the dry mix.
usage: Put a drum sample and a few trigs on T1. On T2 choose NEIGHBOR with FUNC + SRC, then set SLOT to 1.
Set T2 TUNE to 0 with no trig-note transpose, GAIN to 0 dB and LEV to 100. Add a T2 trig and use a long AMP HOLD or DECAY so its envelope lets T1 through.
Play the pattern and adjust T2’s filter or delay send. Lower T1’s AMP VOL to hear only T2’s processed signal; the source tap is before T1’s volume.
Try T2 TUNE at +12 semitones, or lock T2’s trig notes, to pitch-shift the routed audio. The shifter adds latency beyond the routing block.
Stop playback, restore T1’s AMP VOL and set T2 SLOT to 0 to silence the route. Return T2 TUNE to 0 and GAIN to 0 dB for a neutral starting point.

steps: Use a build containing NEIGHBOR for the original Digitakt on OS 1.53 or 1.54, and load a sample on the source track.
Select a different audio track, press FUNC + SRC, scroll below SLICE to NEIGHBOR, and confirm with YES.
On the receiving track’s SRC page set SLOT (knob E) to the source track number, then add a receiving-track trig.

controls.name: TUNE
controls.doc: SRC knob A: pitch shift from -24 to +24 semitones, also transposed by the receiving trig’s note. At 0.00 with no note transpose the shifter is bypassed. Nonzero shifting adds approximately 3–27 ms beyond the routing delay.

controls.name: BR
controls.doc: SRC knob C: stock-style bit reduction applied to the routed signal in the receiving track’s chain.

controls.name: SLOT
controls.doc: SRC knob E: source audio track 1–8. Zero or this receiving track’s own number produces silence. The source is tapped after its filter and before its volume.

controls.name: GAIN
controls.doc: SRC knob F: amplification from 0 to +31.5 dB in 0.5 dB steps after the receiving chain and before its volume. Clips at full scale. Unlike LEV, it does not increase drive into the receiving overdrive.

controls.name: LEV
controls.doc: SRC knob H: level entering the receiving chain, scaled by trig velocity. LEV 100 with velocity 100 passes the source at its own level before the receiving processing; higher values drive its overdrive harder.

limitations: A prototype: the source audio arrives one block (0.67 ms) late.

load.conditions: Measure with every track playing, parameters modulated and the mod at its heaviest setting.

presentation.label: Digi Poly
presentation.summary: A POLY machine: chords from a track’s own trigs, borrowing other tracks’ voices, and polyphonic MIDI on its channel.
presentation.overview: Digi Poly adds a POLY machine to the FUNC+SRC list. A POLY track plays like ONESHOT, but its TRIG page becomes the MIDI tracks’ page, so every trig can carry a chord: NOT1 plays on the track’s own voice and NOT2-NOT4 each borrow the voice of another track. A borrowed voice plays the POLY track’s whole sound, follows its knobs and level, and gets its own sound back at its own next trig. The track’s key plays the chord, notes on its own MIDI channel play polyphonically, and SETTINGS > POLY chooses, per pattern, which tracks lend their voice.
highlights: Chords from a track’s own trigs: NOT1 and up to three extra notes, set for the track or locked per step.
Each extra note borrows the voice whose last note started longest ago, never a muted track, a voice holding a live note or a track with a trig at the same moment.
Pressing the POLY track’s key plays the whole chord.
Notes on the POLY track’s own MIDI channel play polyphonically, one voice per note, and recording writes up to four notes into the step.
SETTINGS > POLY chooses which tracks lend their voice; it is kept in the pattern’s kit and saved with the project.
The track’s LEVEL and its SRC, FLTR, AMP and LFO knobs apply to the whole chord, borrowed voices included.
Several tracks can be POLY; each plays its own chords.
usage: Play chords from one audio track: set NOT2-NOT4 on its TRIG page and let the extra notes borrow other tracks’ voices.
Lock a step’s own chord: hold its trig in grid recording and turn a knob.
Play or record chords from a MIDI keyboard on the POLY track’s own channel; up to four notes land in the step’s NOT1-NOT4.
Take tracks that must never be cut out of the pool in SETTINGS > POLY. Drum tracks that trig often are borrowed last.

steps: On any audio track press FUNC + SRC and choose POLY, after SLICE, with a three-note icon.
Set the chord on the track’s TRIG page: NOT1 and NOT2-NOT4.
Choose which tracks lend their voice in SETTINGS > POLY.

controls.name: NOT1
controls.doc: On a POLY track’s TRIG page: the note, played on the track’s own voice. Set it for the track, or hold a trig in grid recording and turn the knob to lock a step’s own value.

controls.name: NOT2-NOT4
controls.doc: Extra notes as semitone offsets from NOT1; the centre value is off. Each plays on a voice borrowed from another track, and with no voice left the note is skipped. Set them for the track, or lock a step’s own chord.

controls.name: VEL, LEN, PROB, LFO.T
controls.doc: The rest of the MIDI tracks’ TRIG page, which a POLY track shows in place of the audio one. Set them for the track, or lock them per step.

controls.name: LEVEL
controls.doc: On a POLY track’s TRIG page the LEVEL knob sets the track level; the LEV fader beside NOT1 shows it, with the value for a moment after a turn. The track’s LEVEL and every SRC, FLTR, AMP and LFO knob apply to the whole chord, borrowed voices included, while they play its notes.

controls.name: Trig key / FUNC+TRK keyboard
controls.doc: Pressing the POLY track’s key, its trig key or a key of the FUNC+TRK keyboard, plays the whole chord. Only the note you played is recorded; the chord’s other notes go straight to the audio engine and are not sent to MIDI OUT.

controls.name: MIDI in on the track’s channel
controls.doc: Notes on the POLY track’s own MIDI channel play polyphonically, one voice per note: the track’s own voice if it is free, else a borrowed one, and the note-off releases that voice. With the sequencer recording, notes arriving at one step are written as a chord: the lowest in NOT1 and the next three in NOT2-NOT4 as offsets from it. A step that gets a single note plays a single note. No MIDI track or cable setup is needed.

controls.name: LEFT / RIGHT (SETTINGS > POLY)
controls.doc: Choose a track; a bar marks it. The checkbox on the left is ticked while the chosen track is in the pool, and tracks in the pool are shown inverted.

controls.name: YES (SETTINGS > POLY)
controls.doc: Take the chosen track out of the POLY voice pool, or put it back. The pool is part of the pattern’s kit: every pattern can lend different voices, and it is saved with the project and comes back after a power-off. Patterns that share a kit share it, loading a sound onto a track does not change it, and every track starts in the pool.

limitations: elekloader refuses it in one build with NEIGHBOR, DIGISLICER or SOPHIE, because their patch sites overlap.
Built for OS 1.53 and 1.54.
Each extra note borrows another track’s voice: it cuts what that track was playing, and that track’s own next trig cuts the chord note. With no voice left, the extra note is skipped.
POLY is machine 6 since 2.0 (it was 4): a POLY track saved with 1.0f loads as NEIGHBOR or ONESHOT, so choose POLY on it again.
On the stock OS, kits saved with POLY load as ONESHOT. Before reverting, the author advises setting POLY tracks back to ONESHOT and saving again, or restoring a backup.
A lost MIDI note-off leaves a borrowed voice held, and that track’s sequencer trigs are blocked while it is; send the note-off or stop the notes from the sender.

The voice pool is kept in bytes of each sound record that the firmware saves but does not use. The author asks you to back up projects before flashing and to check once, after a power cycle, that a pattern’s pool came back.
The POLY track’s TRIG page is the MIDI tracks’ page shown for an audio track; the author notes that an untested edit path could behave differently from a MIDI track.
The author’s mod also declares a conflict with dt8poly, their earlier POLY mod, which is not in Modwerk.
Not yet tested on a unit, the author reports; it passes their emulator tests on OS 1.53 and 1.54.

load.conditions: Measure with every track playing, a POLY track playing four-note chords on borrowed voices, live MIDI notes on its channel, and its knobs turned while the chords sound.

presentation.label: DIGISLICER
presentation.summary: A slicing machine with a slice editor: cut a sample where you want, and play the slices from the trig keys and the keyboard.
presentation.overview: DIGISLICER adds a separate SRC machine with a waveform slice editor to the original Digitakt. Select it below SLICE, choose a sample and press SRC again to edit starts, create a grid or slice on transients. Custom slices belong to the sample and take precedence over GRID on every DIGISLICER track using it; they are saved to the +Drive after closing the editor. GRID adds AUTO and PLAY adds PIPO for forward/backward looping across the slices covered by LEN. With FUNC + TRK keyboard mode enabled, trig keys play slices at the track’s pitch and can record slice locks. The stock SLICE machine retains its normal behavior.
highlights: Edit up to 64 slices with coarse/fine start adjustment, a cursor and horizontal/vertical waveform zoom.
Use transient AUTO slicing or 4/8/16/32/64-slice grids with starts moved to zero crossings.
Custom slices follow the sample across projects and override GRID on DIGISLICER tracks.
Keyboard mode plays one slice per trig key, with four pages and live recording of slice locks.
PIPO ping-pongs for the note’s duration, including spans of multiple slices set with LEN.
usage: Choose DIGISLICER with FUNC + SRC, assign a drum loop with SAMP, then press SRC again to open its waveform editor.
Press YES for the slice menu, select CREATE GRID with UP / DOWN, choose 16 with LEFT / RIGHT and confirm with YES. This replaces the sample’s existing slice layout.
Select a slice with knob A. Adjust its start with B and fine-tune with C; use D to zoom around the cursor and H to enlarge quiet waveform details.
Close the editor with SRC or NO and wait at least a second for the slices to save. They now play on every DIGISLICER track using this sample, regardless of GRID.
Enable keyboard mode with FUNC + TRK and play the slices from trig keys 1–16. UP / DOWN select later slice pages; REC + PLAY records the played keys as slice locks.
Press STOP and leave recording/keyboard mode when finished. To remove the custom layout, reopen the editor and choose YES → DELETE ALL; playback returns to the SRC page’s GRID setting.

steps: Use a build containing DIGISLICER for the original Digitakt on OS 1.53 or 1.54.
Select an audio track, press FUNC + SRC, choose DIGISLICER below SLICE and select a sample with SAMP.
From the SRC parameter page press SRC again to open the slice editor. SRC or NO closes it; another page key closes it and opens that page.
For slice performance outside the editor, enable keyboard mode with FUNC + TRK. UP / DOWN select groups of 16 slices.

controls.name: Knob A
controls.doc: In the editor, select a slice one per notch; the cursor jumps to its start. In the slice menu, choose an action, then press YES to apply it.

controls.name: Knob B
controls.doc: In the editor, move the selected slice’s start. This edits the shared slice layout for the sample, not only this track.

controls.name: Knob C
controls.doc: In the editor, fine-adjust the selected start one sample at a time.

controls.name: Knob D
controls.doc: In the editor, zoom horizontally around the cursor. Faster turns zoom faster; move the cursor with LEVEL to focus on another region.

controls.name: Knob H
controls.doc: In the editor, enlarge the waveform vertically up to 64 times to inspect quiet material; this changes the view, not the audio level.

controls.name: LEVEL
controls.doc: In the editor, move the waveform cursor; the view scrolls to keep it visible. YES then offers ADD SLICE HERE when a new start is allowed at that position.

controls.name: FUNC + YES
controls.doc: In the editor, run AUTO SLICE on the sample’s transients. This replaces the sample’s existing custom slice layout.

controls.name: YES
controls.doc: Open the slice menu. UP / DOWN or knob A choose ADD SLICE HERE, SPLIT SLICE, DELETE SLICE, AUTO SLICE, CREATE GRID or DELETE ALL; YES applies the action and NO cancels the menu.

controls.name: SAMP
controls.doc: On the SRC page, choose the track’s sample. In the editor, FUNC + LEFT / RIGHT changes the sample slot and updates the track’s SAMP selection.

controls.name: GRID
controls.doc: On the SRC page, select an equal slice grid or AUTO, one step past 64, for transient slices. A sample’s custom slices override this setting; DELETE ALL in the editor restores GRID-based playback.

controls.name: SLICE
controls.doc: On the SRC page, choose the played slice; slice locks sequence different slices. In keyboard mode each trig key chooses its own slice at the track’s pitch, regardless of the current SLICE value.

controls.name: LEN
controls.doc: On the SRC page, choose how many slices a note spans. In PIPO mode the voice turns at the end of the last slice covered by LEN and returns to the first slice’s start.

controls.name: PLAY
controls.doc: On the SRC page, retain the stock playback modes or choose PIPO, one step past FWD, for ping-pong looping while the note lasts. Each new note starts forward; the page shows a bidirectional loop icon.

controls.name: TUNE / BR / LEV
controls.doc: On the SRC page, the stock SLICE-style pitch, bit reduction and source-level controls still apply. Keyboard slice keys keep the track’s pitch; they select slices rather than transpose notes.

controls.name: LEFT / RIGHT
controls.doc: In the editor, select the previous or next slice and audition it while the key is held. In CREATE GRID, choose 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64 slices.

controls.name: Trig keys / UP / DOWN
controls.doc: In the editor, trig keys select and audition slices 1–16 while held; UP / DOWN select later groups up to slice 64. Outside the editor, FUNC + TRK keyboard mode uses the same slice pages; keys beyond the slice count stay dark and silent.

controls.name: FUNC + NO
controls.doc: In the editor, delete the selected slice; its start merges into the preceding slice. Use NO without FUNC to leave the editor and keep the layout.

controls.name: SRC / NO / page keys
controls.doc: SRC or NO closes the editor and keeps the slices; TRIG, FLTR, AMP or LFO closes it and opens that page. Slices are saved to the +Drive about a second later. PLAY and STOP keep their normal transport functions.

controls.name: FUNC + TRK / recording
controls.doc: Outside the editor, FUNC + TRK enables slice keyboard mode. REC + PLAY records played slices as locks. In STEP REC (REC + STOP), FUNC + a trig key writes that slice at the cursor.

limitations: Slices are stored on the +Drive in /cfw/slices.a and /cfw/slices.b; a /cfw folder appears in the sample browser.

presentation.label: SOPHIE
presentation.summary: A metallic percussion machine with four models: FUSE, BOOM, PIPE and SHARD.
presentation.overview: Sophie is a metallic percussion synth machine for the original Digitakt. It began as a fixed-point adaptation of Sophie for Schwung by Matt Estela and evolved into four models: FUSE, BOOM, PIPE and SHARD. Its audio enters the normal Digitakt AMP, filter, mixer and sends; the custom controls can be parameter-locked.
highlights: Four metallic percussion models: FUSE, BOOM, PIPE and SHARD.
FOLD wavefolder with output level compensation.
Uses the Digitakt’s own AMP, filter, mixer and effects.
usage: Program metallic hits and bells with parameter-locked MODEL and METAL.
Use AMP HOLD = NOTE so TRIG LEN sets when the release begins.

steps: Select a track, press FUNC + SRC and choose SOPHIE.
Set the machine’s controls on the SRC page; AMP shapes the note envelope.

controls.name: TUNE
controls.doc: Pitch

controls.name: MODEL
controls.doc: FUSE / BOOM / PIPE / SHARD

controls.name: FOLD
controls.doc: Wavefolder with output level compensation; zero bypasses it

controls.name: SAMP
controls.doc: Stock sample selector; Sophie does not use the sample

controls.name: SWEEP
controls.doc: Bipolar pitch sweep toward the played note

controls.name: METAL
controls.doc: FM/ring intensity

controls.name: FBK
controls.doc: Oscillator feedback

controls.name: COLOR
controls.doc: Inharmonic character

presentation.label: Digi utilities
presentation.summary: Hold "..." for a live scope, spectrum analyser and stereo X-Y view, with a tuner and track activity.
presentation.overview: Digi utilities opens a live utility page over the main screen when you hold the "..." key. Pressing "..." on the page steps through a waveform scope, a spectrum analyser (30 Hz to 20 kHz) and a stereo X-Y view, then closes it. The waveform and spectrum views also show a tuner and activity boxes for all 8 audio tracks. The top bar, mutes, pattern and bank changes, page keys and knobs keep working while the page is open, so you can change a sound and watch it change. A short press of "..." is still the stock Song mode popup. The master EQ that earlier versions carried is now its own mod, Digi EQ.
highlights: Waveform, spectrum and stereo X-Y (goniometer) views on one held key, over the main screen.
Spectrum from 30 Hz to 20 kHz: 128 log columns, about 60 dB tall, with falling peaks and ticks at 100 Hz, 1 kHz and 10 kHz.
Tuner: note, octave and cents (A4 = 440 Hz), from about 12 Hz to 3 kHz.
Activity boxes for all 8 audio tracks flash on each trig; a POLY note held on a voice keeps its box lit.
The top bar, mutes, pattern changes, page keys and knobs keep working while the page is open.
Song mode works as stock: a short press of "..." is the SONG MODE popup.
usage: Solo a track and hold "..." to tune it: the tuner hears the main output, and a chord shows its common root.
Turn a track’s knobs with the page open and watch the waveform or the spectrum change.
Check stereo width and phase on the X-Y view: mono is a vertical line, left only "\", right only "/", out of phase horizontal and wide a cloud.

access.location: A utility page over the main screen, opened by holding the "..." key
steps: Hold the "..." (three dots) key for about half a second; a short press is still the SONG MODE popup.
Press "..." again to go from the waveform to the spectrum and to X-Y; the next press closes the page.
Press YES for fullscreen; NO closes the page.

controls.name: Hold "..."
controls.doc: Holding the “...” (three dots) key, without FUNC, for about half a second opens the utility page on the waveform view. A short press is the stock SONG MODE popup, so Song mode works as on the official OS (popup, EDIT, double press).

controls.name: "..." on the page
controls.doc: Steps from the waveform to the spectrum, then to X-Y; the next press closes the page.

controls.name: YES
controls.doc: Fullscreen on and off: the main view only, with no overlays; the top bar is hidden.

controls.name: NO
controls.doc: Closes the page.

controls.name: PTN / BANK + trig
controls.doc: Changes pattern; the page stays open and the green LEDs show the patterns with data.

controls.name: Knobs
controls.doc: Edit the parameters of the page selected underneath (TRIG, SRC, FLTR, AMP or LFO) while the utility page covers it, so you can change a sound and watch it; close the page to read the values.

controls.name: Mutes, page keys, PLAY/STOP, FUNC
controls.doc: Mutes, page keys, PLAY/STOP and FUNC combinations work as on the main screen while the page is open.

limitations: Modwerk’s builder refuses no mod beside it: in elekloader’s check it combines with every other Modwerk mod for its OS, NEIGHBOR, DIGISLICER and SOPHIE included (SOPHIE is built for OS 1.53 only).
Built for OS 1.53 and 1.54.
The tuner hears the main output, so solo a track to tune it; it shows -- when there is no clear pitch or the sound is too quiet.
With the page open, the knobs edit the page hidden behind it; close the page to read the values.

The spectrum (6 KB) and the tuner (1 KB) each take a buffer from the firmware’s memory once; if that fails, the spectrum stays blank or the tuner is disabled. Both run in the UI task, so the screen may feel slightly slower with the page open.

The page is built from the firmware’s Song edit screen. The author notes that a firmware path treating it as the real Song edit screen could act on it; the Song edit screen opened from the popup stays stock (checked in emulation).
Its author reports the stand-alone 1.5d tested on a Digitakt mk1, and 1.9a not yet; it passes their emulator tests on OS 1.53 and 1.54.

presentation.label: DIGIHEALTH
presentation.summary: SYSTEM INFO shows CPU, DSP and free RAM in the top bar.
presentation.overview: A SETTINGS row, SYSTEM INFO: CPU load, the audio render’s load (the main CPU’s effects and mix; the FM voices run on the second CPU) and free RAM in the top bar, and a read-only USB diagnostics channel (SysEx device 0x7D). FAST AUDIO is Digitakt only.
highlights: CPU, render load and free RAM in the top bar.
A read-only USB diagnostics channel.
usage: Watch the render load while layering FM tracks.

steps: Open SETTINGS.

presentation.label: digitables
presentation.summary: Pitch tables for every note: arpeggios, trills and riffs from one trig, and ADD steps that strum chords.
presentation.overview: M8-style pitch tables for the Digitone mk1. The project holds 16 tables of up to 16 semitone steps, each with a length and a loop point. A sound with a table on plays every note through it: each note restarts the table and the sequencer’s clock steps it, from a slow walk to 1500 steps a second, so one trig plays an arpeggio, a trill, a pitch drop or a riff. A step can ADD a note instead of moving the pitch, so one trig can strum a chord. The TBL page has two knobs, TBL and SPD; hold a track key there for the table editor.
highlights: 16 tables of up to 16 semitone steps, each with a length and a loop point, saved with the project.
TBL and SPD are sound parameters: saved with the kit and p-lockable per trig.
Speeds from 24 ticks a step down to a step every audio block (MAX, 1500 a second, at any tempo).
ADD steps start a copy of the trig’s note at the step’s offset: a strummed chord from one trig.
A full-screen table editor whose edits sound at once, even on a note already playing.
A project saved with digitables loads on the stock OS, which ignores the tables and keeps them through a save.
usage: A C64 chord: in table 2, steps 0, +4, +7, length 3, loop 1; TBL 2 and SPD 1 on a bright sound with a short release, and hold a long note. Minor: 0, +3, +7.
A strum: in table 3, steps 0, +4, +7, +12 with ADD on steps 2–4, length 4, loop OFF; TBL 3 and SPD 1 or 1/2 on a plucky sound. Every note becomes a major chord strummed upward.
Strum down by starting high and adding downward: +12, +7 ADD, +4 ADD, 0 ADD.
At SPD 1/16 to MAX, small offsets (0, +1, or 0, +12) turn into vibrato and FM-like buzz.
P-lock TBL or SPD on a trig to play another table, none, or another speed.

access.location: The TBL page: AMP’s third page, or TABLES in the Mod Menu
steps: Hold a track key (T1–T4) on its own for about half a second to open the Mod Menu, and pick TABLES with YES (or trig key 1).
Or press AMP until its third page, TBL, shows.
On the TBL page, hold a track key to open the table editor; NO, or holding a track key again, goes back to the TBL page.

controls.name: A: TBL
controls.doc: The sound’s table: OFF, or 1–16. A sound parameter: saved with the kit, shown and edited like the stock ones, and p-lockable per trig (hold a trig in grid recording and turn the knob).

controls.name: B: SPD
controls.doc: The table’s speed: ticks of the 24 PPQN clock a step, 1–24 (6 is a 16th, 24 a quarter note), and faster to the left of 1: a step every 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/6, 1/8, 1/12, 1/16, 1/24 or 1/32 of a tick, and MAX, a step every audio block (1500 a second, at any tempo). At 120 BPM, 1 is 48 steps a second and 1/16 is 768. P-lockable; turning it while a note plays changes its speed from the next step.

controls.name: TABLES (Mod Menu)
controls.doc: Opens the TBL page. Hold a track key (T1–T4) on its own for about half a second for the Mod Menu, then pick TABLES with YES or trig key 1.

controls.name: Hold a track key (TBL page)
controls.doc: Opens the table editor on the table the track’s sound plays. The editor shows the table’s 16 steps as bars around a zero line; a marker under a step follows a note playing that table. PLAY, STOP, FUNC and the track keys still work while it is open.

controls.name: Editor: trig keys 1–16, LEFT/RIGHT
controls.doc: Pick a step.

controls.name: Editor: A, UP/DOWN
controls.doc: The step’s offset, -48 to +48 semitones; FUNC + UP/DOWN moves it an octave. Edits sound at once, even on a note already playing.

controls.name: Editor: B
controls.doc: The step.

controls.name: Editor: C
controls.doc: The table’s length, 1–16.

controls.name: Editor: D
controls.doc: The loop point: OFF (the last step holds), or 1 up to the length.

controls.name: Editor: H
controls.doc: Which table, 1–16.

controls.name: Editor: YES
controls.doc: The step adds a note (ADD), or not; an ADD step is drawn hollow. When the table reaches an ADD step, the note keeps its pitch and a copy of the trig’s note (its sound, p-locks, velocity and length) starts at the note’s pitch plus the step’s offset, released together with the note that added it. Step 1 always sets the note’s own pitch; marked ADD, it adds a note only when a loop comes back to it.

controls.name: Editor: NO, or hold a track key
controls.doc: Back to the TBL page.

controls.name: Editor: a page key
controls.doc: TRIG, SYN1, SYN2, FLTR, AMP or LFO: leaves the editor for that page.

limitations: The builder refuses no mod beside it: in elekloader’s check it combines with every other Modwerk mod for Digitone OS 1.43. The author checked that it links with digihealth 1.1, but has not run the two together.
It needs the Digitone core 2.2 (core-dn1 2.2) for its parameter slots, mod page, project data and Mod Menu entry; core 2.2 is then the one every Digitone OS 1.43 build uses.
Built for Digitone OS 1.43 only; the author has not ported it to OS 1.44. The Digitone Keys runs the same OS file but has not been tried.
The tables restored at power-up are unchecked: the Digitone keeps a working copy of the project for power-up, which the author’s emulator cannot show.
The arpeggiator and portamento have not been tried with tables. On a note the arpeggiator plays, ADD steps add nothing.

ADD steps use voices: the Digitone has 8, shared by the four tracks, and an added note takes one like any note, stealing the oldest when none is free. A loop over ADD steps adds notes over and over. An added note is skipped when the firmware’s note pool is short.

The author reports testing v1.3 on a Digitone mk1 (3–4 October 2026): the TBL page, the table editor, the fast speeds, the Mod Menu and ADD steps. Not yet checked: the tables restored at power-up, and the arpeggiator with tables. That report is for the author’s own build.
SPD MAX steps once every audio block, 1500 times a second at any tempo: the one setting that does not follow the sequencer's tempo, by design. Every other SPD value counts ticks of the 24 PPQN clock.

load.conditions: Measure with all four synth tracks playing notes through tables at SPD MAX, and with looping ADD steps keeping all eight voices busy.

tests.summary: Modwerk’s builder linked and verified a build of the author’s v1.3 source with core 2.2 for OS 1.43; nothing was flashed or tested on hardware in Modwerk, and evidence is none.
